name: Familial Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Familial Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of thoracic aortic aneurysm or dissection in two or more first-degree relatives
Imaging evidence of progressive dilation of the thoracic aorta exceeding normal age and body size parameters
Identification of pathogenic mutation in genes associated with familial thoracic aortic aneurysm (e.g., TGFBR1, TGFBR2, ACTA2)
Lack of systemic features suggestive of syndromic aortopathies such as Marfan or Loeys-Dietz syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of thoracic aortic aneurysm in at least two first-degree relatives or aortic dilation with a pathogenic mutation in a relevant gene
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of syndromic causes of thoracic aortic aneurysm.

pathognomonic.notes: Detected by imaging modalities such as echocardiography or CT angiography

pathognomonic.symptomName: Familial clustering of thoracic aortic aneurysm or dissection
searchTerms: family history of chest aorta aneurysm or rupture
familial clustering of aortic aneurysm or dissection

common.notes: Often due to aneurysm expansion or impending dissection
May result from compression of adjacent structures
Due to arrhythmias secondary to aortic root involvement
Common comorbidity that may exacerbate aneurysm progression

occasional.notes: Due to recurrent laryngeal nerve compression by aneurysm
Compression of esophagus by enlarged aorta
May indicate aneurysm expansion or dissection
Possible transient ischemia from aortic pathology

rare.notes: Embolic events secondary to aortic pathology
Due to aortic valve insufficiency or dissection

laboratory: Genetic testing revealing pathogenic variants in TGFBR1, TGFBR2, ACTA2, or related genes
imaging: CT angiography or MRI confirming aneurysm size and extent
Aortic root enlargement without systemic features of syndromic aortopathies
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in genes such as TGFBR1, TGFBR2, ACTA2, MYH11
other: Family history of thoracic aortic aneurysm or dissection
Absence of systemic connective tissue disorder features

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic connective tissue features (e.g., lens dislocation, skeletal abnormalities)
Arterial tortuosity and aneurysms throughout vascular tree
Mutations in TGFBR1 or TGFBR2 with systemic involvement

redFlags: Sudden severe chest or back pain suggestive of aortic dissection
Rapid increase in aortic diameter on serial imaging
Family history of sudden unexplained death or aortic rupture
references: Loeys BL, et al. The revised Ghent nosology for the Marfan syndrome. J Med Genet. 2010.
Milewicz DM, et al. Genetic basis of thoracic aortic aneurysms and dissections: focus on smooth muscle cell contractile dysfunction. Annu Rev Genomics Hum Genet. 2008.
Isselbacher EM. Thoracic and abdominal aortic aneurysms. Circulation. 2005.
